domain_restrictions: the product index i ranges over integers with 1 <= i <= d
when d = 0, the product is the empty product and is defined to be 1
mu_n(C,d) counts elements i in the set {1, ..., d} such that n divides C + i
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: For fixed integers A and B and nonnegative integer d satisfying A >= B >= 0, define Q(q) as the product over i from 1 to d of (1 minus q to the power (A plus i)) divided by (1 minus q to the power (B plus i)), with the convention that when d = 0 the product equals 1. For each positive integer n and integer C define mu_n(C,d) as the number of i in {1, ..., d} such that n divides C plus i. Then Q(q) is a polynomial in q with rational coefficients (belongs to Q[q]) if and only if for every positive integer n, mu_n(B,d) is at most mu_n(A,d).
quantifier_order: Let A, B, d be integers with constraints A >= B >= 0 and d >= 0.
Define Q(q) using the product from i = 1 to d, with the empty product equal to 1 when d = 0.
Define mu_n(C,d) for each positive integer n.
Claim: Q(q) is in Q[q] if and only if for every positive integer n, mu_n(B,d) is <= mu_n(A,d).

witness_dependencies: No existential witnesses are introduced; the condition uses only universal quantification over positive integers n.
The index i used inside mu_n and inside the product is local to those definitions.
The counting function mu_n(B,d) and mu_n(A,d) depend only on the fixed parameters A, B, and d and on the universally quantified n.

statement_nl: Let A,B,d be integers with A >= B >= 0 and d >= 0, and define Q(q) := prod_{i=1}^d (1 - q^(A+i)) / (1 - q^(B+i)), with the empty product equal to 1 if d=0. For each positive integer n define mu_n(C,d) := #{ i in {1,...,d} : n divides C+i }. Then Q(q) belongs to Q[q] if and only if mu_n(B,d) <= mu_n(A,d) for every positive integer n.
